title: Meet Git Gud
subtitle: A Git client with a lane-colored commit graph

sections.title: What Git Gud is
sections.intent: Say what it is, name the four apps, and say what the series covers.

lines.say: This is Git Gud. It's a desktop Git client built around one idea: you should be able to see your history.

props.title: Git Gud
props.subtitle: A Git client you can see through

lines.say: Every branch gets its own colored lane, and everything you do runs as a plain git command you can read.
lines.show: The commit graph of the demo repo, scrolling.

lines.say: Git Gud is a family of four apps. The desktop app is the one you'll use most.
A headless daemon serves repositories from a server with no screen. A relay lets your devices reach each other from anywhere.
lines.show: Diagram highlights the daemon and relay.

lines.say: And a companion app puts your repositories on your phone.

sections.title: Opening a repository
sections.intent: Start page, open a repo, tabs.

lines.say: When you start Git Gud, you land on the start page. Open Repository picks any folder with a git repository in it.
Each repository opens in its own tab. The home button takes you back to the start page, where your recent repositories wait.
Close the app and your tabs come back next time, exactly as you left them.

sections.title: A tour of the window
sections.intent: Name each region of the main window.

lines.say: Here's the main window. In the middle is the commit graph: one row per commit, newest at the top.
On the left, the sidebar lists your branches, remote branches, stashes, worktrees and tags.
Under them sit the power tools: bisect, patch, reflog and clean. We'll get to each one.
On the right is the detail panel. With nothing selected, it shows your uncommitted changes and the commit box.
Select a commit and the same panel shows that commit instead: its message, author, and the files it changed.
Across the top, the toolbar has fetch, pull and push, stash and pop, and a new branch button. The pill in the middle is the branch you're on.
At the bottom is the console dock. One half is a shell. The other half is the git activity log, which shows every command the app runs for you.
This series walks through everything Git Gud does, one episode per area.

props.title: Everything Git Gud does
props.items:
GitCommit | The commit graph | Lanes, refs, search
Plus | Staging and committing | Files, hunks, single lines
GitBranch | Branches and stashes | Tags, worktrees, drag and drop
CloudUpload | Remotes | Fetch, pull, push, sign-in
Scissors | Rewriting history | Rebase, squash, reset
Swords | Conflicts | Conflict editor, auto-fix
LifeBuoy | Recovery tools | Reflog, bisect, patch, clean
Eye | Gerrit mode | Push for review
Settings | Settings and updates | Channels, contrast
Link | Peer connections | Drive another machine
Server | Headless and relay | Linux daemon, rendezvous
Smartphone | Companion app | Your repos on your phone

lines.say: The demo repository is tidepool, a small tide chart app with a few weeks of history from four people. Let's look at its graph.
